title: A Multi‐Model Intelligent Assessment Framework for Temporary Median Opening Design in Expressway Reconstruction and Expansion
content:
A multi-model intelligent framework integrating VISSIM simulation, CRITIC weighting, and four parallel assessment modules evaluates temporary median opening lengths in expressway reconstruction and expansion. Comparative and cross-validation analysis confirms its effectiveness, with 100 m recommended for most scenarios, reducing single-model bias.


ABSTRACT

In response to the lack of a systematic, data-driven evaluation method for the length of temporary median openings in expressway reconstruction and expansion, this study develops an intelligent assessment framework that integrates VISSIM based on microscopic simulation, CRITIC objective weighting, and four parallel assessment modules: TOPSIS, One-Dimensional Cloud Model, MDCM and MDFICM. Three typical opening configurations-lane reduction, lane expansion, and lane conservation-are evaluated under low, medium, and high saturation levels with opening lengths of 100 m, 200 m, and 300 m. Four performance indicators-delay, conflict rate, speed difference, and fuel consumption-are extracted from simulation monitoring. Cross-validation revealed that in the lane conservation scenario, all four modules unanimously recommended 100 m across all saturation levels; in the lane reduction scenario, optimal lengths varied by saturation, i.e., 100 m was recommended under low and high saturation, while 300 m was preferred under medium saturation; in the lane expansion scenario, all four modules consistently recommended 100 m under medium saturation, whereas recommendations diverged under low and high saturation; at low saturation, 100 m received the greatest support (2 of 4 modules) without a majority consensus, while at high saturation, 100 m was supported by three of the four modules. The parallel multi-module architecture effectively mitigates single-model bias by enabling cross-validation from complementary theoretical perspectives. The proposed framework provides a robust, data-driven decision-support tool for temporary traffic organization design in expressway reconstruction and expansion.
